    The Advisor has no language model

    It is installed and answering. Without a model it still reads this node, still plans, and still keeps its ledger; what it cannot do is answer a question in your words.

    Set one up in Settings & Updates, under Advisor AI model: pick a provider, paste a key, choose a model, seal it with your passkey. About a minute. The key is tested against the provider before anything is sealed, and sealed to this host with the system keyring.

    The install command opened a fifteen-minute window for that seal. Settings says whether it is still open, and the line that reopens it.

    Alternative: in a terminal on this host, as aperire: curl -fsSL https://get.aperire.one | bash, answer Y, then 3) Advisor, then 6) Set up / change the model.

    The Advisor

    The Advisor is an optional service that runs beside this dashboard on this host. It reads the node's state, explains what it finds in plain terms, and can carry out a small set of named operations behind a passkey. It is not installed here.

    One command adds it to a host that already runs the dashboard. Run it on this host, over SSH or at the console:

    curl -fsSL https://get.aperire.one/advisor | bash

    It finds the install already on this box, builds the Advisor, starts it on its own account, and reads the service back before telling you it worked. Then it points you back here to set up a language model.

    Would rather not pipe a URL into a shell? Download and read it first with curl -fsSL https://get.aperire.one/advisor -o get-advisor.sh, or use the operator menu on this host: bash $HOME/aperire-one, then 3) Advisor, then 1) Install the Advisor on this host.

    The dashboard notices on its own once it answers. There is no flag to set and nothing to reinstall: the Advisor tab and everything that links to it come back by themselves.

    The setup guide covers the model, the privileged account and the rest: docs/ADVISOR-SETUP.md

    Operations

    Where operations run Every act this Advisor carries out plays out here — an upgrade, a restart, a configuration change, a rollback. The heading names whichever one is running or has just run, and goes back to OPERATIONS when the node is settled and nothing is in flight. An upgrade is the one act that offers itself: when this node’s registry has a newer release than it runs, the plan appears here and is approved with its confirm code and your passkey. Every other act is asked for in chat, inside a break-glass window, and its transcript arrives in this panel. With nothing in flight the badge counts every run this node has on record, and Run history at the bottom of the panel opens each one to its transcript. checking the node… ▾

    Run history What has actually been done Every privileged run on this node, upgrades, restarts, configuration changes and rollbacks, with the full step-by-step transcript exactly as it ran. Read live from the node’s own Advisor service, held nowhere in between, so what you read here is what that host did, not a copy.     Your node’s setup

    Knowledge

    Curating the Advisor’s knowledge Lessons the fleet’s Advisors propose from their own investigations. Adding one files it into the retrieval-augmented (RAG) knowledge base every Advisor answers from — reviewed by you, pushed to every node, cited as Documented. Rejecting records why, so a repeat proposal says it was rejected before. This curation is what makes the Aperire One Advisor sharper over time. 1 of 1
    Base knowledge reading…
    Fleet memory What every node's Advisor remembers Read whole from each node's own memory and inbox and kept here, named to the node it came from. A poll that cannot reach a node leaves what is already held exactly as it was, so this can be behind, never wrong. Promoting an entry copies it into fleet knowledge, on your word alone, nothing here reaches another node by itself.

    Audit trail

    The record that cannot be quietly edited The node’s own ledger: every break-glass window, gated question, proposal, approval and run, each entry hash-chained to the one before and verified end to end every time this loads. “Unbroken” is that verification passing — an edited or deleted entry would break the chain and be called out here, loudly.
      Advisor
      Let the Advisor dig deeper. Opens a 15-minute window in which it may read more of this host: configuration, logs, resource state. Never key material. You approve it with a passkey; every read inside it is recorded, and you can exit it early.
